title: “They Sent from There”
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Sanhedrin 17b identifies this expression with Rabbi Elazar. It occurs in Gittin 20a; Bava Batra 126b and 158b; Chullin 92a; and Menachot 43a. In some places it is not Rabbi Elazar, as in Bava Batra 174b: “They sent from there: If they placed him under a ban and he died under that ban, the law follows Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua”; and Zevachim 87a: “The law follows Rav Yosef.” Perhaps the expression there belongs to the Gemara’s anonymous voice, for by Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua’s time there were no longer academies in the Land of Israel.

notes.text: Hyman’s chronology of the academies and possible anonymous-Gemara explanation remain his claims. The two occurrences of Huna son of Yehoshua refer to the same connected name.

Sanhedrin 17b first assigns “they sent from there” to Yose bar Chanina and then reverses it to Rabbi Elazar. Bava Batra 174b directly contains the ruling following Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. These textual parallels do not independently establish Hyman’s account of the academies.
